title: Lee So-young's return keeps the "Four Attackers" alive; IBK Industrial Bank of Korea defeats defending champion GS Caltex to secure second consecutive win [V-League] - 스타뉴스
content:
Hwaseong IBK Industrial Bank of Korea extended its winning streak to two games by also defeating "defending champion" Seoul GS Caltex. IBK Industrial Bank of Korea defeated GS Caltex with a set score of 3-1 (28-26, 25-19, 25-27, 25-21) in the home game of the women's division of the 2026-2027 HK Hieunguk Financial V-League held at Hwaseong Comprehensive Gymnasium on the 6th. IBK Industrial Bank of Korea, which won against Suwon Hyundai E&C in the opening match on the 3rd, rode a rising momentum by also defeating GS Caltex, who had topped both last season's championship and the Cup tournament. GS Caltex suffered a loss after its first win. For IBK Industrial Bank of Korea, foreign main attacker Victoria Danchev (registered name: Victoria), who recorded the highest points among both teams, scored 25 points; middle blocker Choi Jung-min, who blocked six times, contributed 23 points; another middle blocker Lee Ju-ah added 17 points; and outside hitter Osanai Miwako (registered name: Miwa) chipped in with 14 points. Unforced errors reached 24, more than Hyundai E&C (16), and IBK did not hold a significant advantage in blocks (15-12). There was also no major difference in serves (4-3) and attack success rate (39.53%-34.62%). The difference between the two teams was decided by attack efficiency (29.07%-19.87%), which hinged on defense, including serve reception. At the center of this was the returning ace, Lee So-young. Lee So-young, who transferred to IBK Industrial Bank of Korea with a total compensation of 700 million won ahead of the 2024-2025 season, could not play in many matches due to injury. Her shoulder injury worsened further next season, leading her to undergo surgery last November. Lee So-young, who felt an immense burden of failing to justify her market value, requested contract termination from the club. She could not become a "bailout" (a player who leaves after receiving high compensation). As a high-earning player, she was determined to reduce the club's financial burden while returning only when she was in a definite physical condition. Although she is still not at 100% physical condition, Lee So-young is contributing significantly to defense with a diligent attitude. Of the six points she scored on this day, three were from attacks, three were blocks, and the rest were contributions from defense. Her reception efficiency reached an impressive 62.29%. This was much higher than libero Im Myeong-ok (33.33%), and she even succeeded in 19 digs, more than Im Myeong-ok (18). Lee So-young solidly guarded the back row alongside Im Myeong-ok, providing a foundation that allowed setters to distribute the ball with confidence. Kim Ha-kyung and Park Eun-seo increased the utilization frequency of Victoria (usage rate 32.56%), Miwa (23.26%), as well as Choi Jung-min (18.6%) and Lee Ju-ah (17.44%), shaking up GS Caltex's defensive line. This also became a factor that lowered the attack efficiency of GS Caltex's main attacker Silva to 15.52%. IBK Industrial Bank of Korea, which was leading 23-20 in the first set, faced the danger of losing the set after conceding four consecutive points, but ultimately forced a deuce and took the first set with a score of 26-26 thanks to Silva's consecutive unforced errors. In the second set, despite committing as many as 10 unforced errors, IBK held on stably, with Lee So-young recording a 100% reception efficiency. Kim Ha-kyung utilized various attack routes and secured another win with efficient attacks. IBK Industrial Bank of Korea, which narrowly lost the third set after a deuce, widened the score gap in the fourth set starting with Lee So-young's quick open point. Through bold attacks enabled by Lee So-young's stable reception, they extended the lead, and with Lee So-young's block also hitting its mark, they stretched the score from 7-7 to 12-8. They then maintained their lead consistently to ultimately secure the victory. In the men's division match held at Incheon Gyeoyang Gymnasium, Suwon KEPCO staged an upset by defeating Incheon Korean Air, who achieved a double title last season, with a set score of 3-1 (25-23, 18-25, 26-24, 27-25). The difference was decided by concentration in crucial moments. KEPCO created a set point at 23-23 in the first set with an open attack by Sharon Vernon Evans (registered name: Sho), and took the first set on Korean Air's hit error. After losing the second set, KEPCO was trailing 23-24 in the third set when Yoon Ha-jun scored a quick open point and then smiled after recording two consecutive service aces. In the fourth set, they were again in danger at 23-24, but KEPCO entered a deuce with Sho's back attack and decorated the victory with Lee Min-gyu's block and Sho's finishing touch. KEPCO, led by Sho with 26 points and Yoon Ha-jun with 14 points in team attacks, secured one win after one loss. title: Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Jan Hatzius Joins CNBC to Discuss the US Jobs Report and the Economic Outlook - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The recent stronger-than-expected employment report indicates a stable labor market, according to Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Jan Hatzius. He joined CNBC to discuss his views on the data and his outlook for the year ahead. Host: Welcome back. The October jobs number came in hotter than expected: nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, above nearly every forecast. Joining us is Jan Hatzius, Goldman Sachs Chief Economist, to discuss the report, the midterms, markets, data centers, and more. Jan, it is great to have you. Host: There is nothing wrong with this number, I assume you agree. Do you think it marks the beginning of something new? Jan Hatzius: Definitely nothing wrong with it. It is a very solid report, certainly as far as payrolls are concerned. There is some month-to-month volatility, but we think the underlying trend in job growth is probably back above 100,000. That is more solid than it was earlier in the year. What we are not seeing is sustained downward pressure on the unemployment rate. It edged down a little, but it has remained in the 4.1% to 4.2% range. To me, this still looks like a labor market that is stable at about full employment. We think it will probably stay roughly in that range over time, which remains consistent with relatively subdued wage growth and low inflation. Host: How low can claims get? Are we scraping the bottom of that historic range? Jan Hatzius: It is the lowest we have seen in a series that goes back more than five decades. Layoffs are at extremely low levels, which is consistent with what we see in other indicators. Hiring continues to be relatively subdued as well, so we have not really seen a major pickup in hiring. It is still a more stagnant environment, but at a very solid level. Host: The markets this week have been rethinking the possibility of a more elongated buildout cycle. Does that lead you to lower your nominal GDP estimates for next year? Jan Hatzius: We are growing at a very rapid pace right now. GDP numbers fluctuate, but we are talking about growth with a three-handle in the second and third quarters, and likely in the fourth quarter as well. I do think growth will be softer next year. We have thought that before, but we have not made a change to our underlying growth estimate. We think it is probably in the 2% to 2.5% range, which should keep the unemployment rate roughly stable. There are some downside risks to that growth outlook. We have seen tightening in financial conditions of about 50 basis points according to our index. There are also questions around energy prices, the war with Iran and its implications for real income growth, as well as the AI buildout and its effects on both GDP and the labor market. Host: Goldman also closely monitors increases in enterprise efficiency from AI use, or at least expected productivity gains. Where are we now, and what are your expectations for 2027? Jan Hatzius: We have seen some effects on the labor market, mainly in the technology sector. That has been worth roughly 10,000 to 15,000 fewer jobs per month in employment growth. There are some indications that this is broadening into the service sector. For example, we have begun to see a correlation across service-sector industries between employment growth and unemployment rates on one hand, and AI adoption on the other. But the relationship is still not particularly strong, and you would not expect it to be if you looked at overall labor-market outcomes. Over the next year or two, I think that relationship will probably strengthen. By 2028, it is likely to become somewhat more of a headwind for employment growth. I have a fair amount of conviction that AI will be more of a macroeconomic story by 2027, though the timing remains one of the open questions. Jan Hatzius: Yes, although at the moment it is clearly still a tailwind. Once we get into 2028, you would expect the volume of investment to flatten out, and eventually investment spending will come down. That is what tends to happen in historical investment booms: infrastructure is built out, the necessary capital stock is achieved, and investment then begins to decline. That is probably still some way off, but there is, of course, substantial uncertainty around the path. Host: We are glad we will have you around for 2027 and 2028. I hope we will speak many times. title: The US Midterms: Reshaping the Stock Market - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The US midterm elections could strengthen the stock market rotation that was already underway, says Lou Miller, global head of Custom Basket Trading in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Traditional defensive sectors such as consumer staples are expensive right now, but healthcare stocks may provide defense along with earnings acceleration, Miller explains on The Markets podcast. He also says that stocks related to the data-center buildout have fallen sharply, resetting valuations and lowering the bar for positive surprises. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, November 5th, and we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Lou Miller, who is our global head of our custom baskets business within FICC and Equities. And on the back of the midterm elections, we're going to explore the market reaction and where we go from here. Chris Hussey: Let's start with the rotation trade that you can see from your baskets group. In particular, that there was a rotation already happening before the midterms. How is that evolving post midterms? Where do you think it heads into the year end? Lou Miller: Yeah, so we've seen, especially in the second half of the year, it's been a really challenging environment for active investors, and we've seen people get very defensive. If you look at beta-adjusted net exposure in our prime book, it's definitely at very low levels versus history. Chris Hussey: Let me peel back the onion a little bit on the rotation. Let's talk about data centers if we can. How is that data center trade holding up in the post-election world? Lou Miller: Worse than I would've thought. I think it's bigger picture concerns like ROI, open-source competition, limits on capital markets came into picture the last few months. The AI data center trade, the right tail of that trade has increasingly gotten removed, and multiples have dramatically dropped to much healthier levels. We now see data center stocks down 36% from their highs earlier this year. And then some of the higher beta areas like memory down 42%, optical networking down 46%, even NeoCloud's down 57%. So the early reaction was way more extreme than I would've expected, but I think the silver lining is the bar is much, much lower for surprises and there are positive catalysts ahead. Think about this: the multiple for the data center trade is about half of what it was in June. We're at liberation day lows in terms of multiples. So you can't argue valuation is a headwind anymore, and there are some positive catalysts ahead. Chris Hussey: Okay. I want to dive now into a little bit of a comment you made about defensives, and I want to go back to the post-pandemic era where tech became the new defensives. Let's explore the AI trade more broadly. You talked about a rotation. You talked about the data center trade. What about the AI trade more broadly? Is that a new defensive kind of trade, or is that really evolving? Lou Miller: I think the next leg of the AI trade is actually healthcare, and I think that's also a very defensive sector that historically is very uncorrelated to AI. Healthcare, we notice those companies are getting very involved at, like, the tools and diagnostics level and that there's now we're going from headwinds to tailwinds there. There's both cyclical and secular drivers there and it's really one of the few sectors that we're going to see accelerating growth next year. AI touches a lot of different parts of the economy, a lot of different parts of the market everything from the application layer, like cybersecurity, but I think healthcare is an area that increasingly looks more and more credible. Chris Hussey: All right. If the new defensives aren't the new defensive, what is the new defensive? What do you want to play defense? Lou Miller: So yeah. So expensive defensives I don't think are defensive. Lou Miller: In a slowing growth environment, not just for the AI CapEx complex, but the real economy it does make sense to be defensive, but you don't want to take it too far. You don't want to bury your head in the sand. So you take staples, for example, the earnings yield of staples is half of the high yield bond yield. The dividend yield of staples is half of the 10-year treasury yield. To me, that's not a good deal for investors. I think people should look beyond the traditional defensive label and look for other characteristics, like quality or free cash flow yield or earnings yield in this higher nominal growth backdrop. I think those dynamics are going to be a lot more defensive than a traditional defensive like staples. Chris Hussey: All right, great. So, we've walked through it. We've walked through the AI trade, the data center trade, the expensive defensives. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Lou Miller: I think the S&P 500 excluding AI is the trade. So rather than pay 25 times earnings for some, you know, boring consumer product, you can pay a high teen multiple for low teens earnings growth. These are some of the highest quality balance sheets in the market. You're buying quality compounders in a decelerating growth environment. That seems like a safe play here over the next six months. Chris Hussey: I'm just curious, if you buy the S&P ex AI, how many stocks is that? Lou Miller: Well, you can, you can get about 500 if you- Just got to add a few extra. Chris Hussey: I like that. I love that. All right. As we go deeper into the end of the year, what are you watching for? Lou Miller: Employment, inflation, the geopolitical events that have passed, and then the rest of earnings season. Those are key. And then longer term, I'm watching the equity capital markets quite closely, debt capital markets closely, and then the FOMC decision on December 9th. Chris Hussey: I know it's early yet, but I've already gotten some Hallmark ads in front of me. Chris Hussey: Oh, a relaxed Santa Rally. I like myself a relaxed Santa. Lou, thanks so much for joining us. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: Karol G’s Ex Anuel AA Says She Still Has Him Blocked on Social Media - AOL.com
content: Anuel AA said he was joking about asking Karol G to unblock him on social media and hasn’t actually done it The former couple ended their two-year engagement in 2021 after first meeting on a music video set Karol G previously said her album Mañana Será Bonito helped her heal after their split Karol G is seemingly keeping her social media ex-free. On Friday, Nov. 6, Anuel AA sat down with Billboard to discuss his upcoming music —and he was asked about his relationship with a superstar ex. In the past, the Puerto Rican rapper has publicly discussed that Karol has him blocked on social media. While promoting his song “Vuelve” (Spanish for “return”) in October, Anuel wrote a plea for his ex in the caption. “RETURN KAROL G. UNBLOCK ME BB. IT’S NOT THAT I’M A PLAYER. IT’S THAT I FALL DEEPLY IN LOVE,” he wrote on Instagram in Spanish. In his interview with Billboard, Anuel was asked if he had seriously asked her to unblock him yet. “No, I’m just messing with her. But maybe she’ll unblock me,” Anuel said. When asked if he wishes for all of his exes to be at peace with him, he said “not all of them.” “We should live in peace, right?” he said, adding that if a movie was made about his love life, it would be called Anuel’s Love’s a Bitch. “It’ll sell a lot. It’ll be incredible.” Anuel — who’s gearing up to release Real Hasta La Muerte 2 (RHLM 2) and a Mexican corridos album this month — and Karol first met in 2018 on the set of their “Culpables” music video. The pair went on to announce they were dating in November 2018 and announced their engagement in April 2019. After a two-year engagement, Anuel and Karol called it quits in April 2021, announcing their breakup on social media. “If just accepting it is hard enough, imagine having to do it in front of millions of people,” Karol wrote in Spanish on her Instagram Story at the time. “For a long time we tried to keep our relationship away from social media in order to protect ourselves. We never used our relationship for marketing purposes, not today, not even almost three years ago when we started [dating].” Months after they ended their engagement, Karol and Anuel reunited on stage at the end of her Bichota Tour and the “Tusa” singer said she would “always admire” him on social media afterward. In July 2024, Karol told PEOPLE that her fourth studio album, Mañana Será Bonito, was her attempting to “heal my heart” from their split.

title: 2026 Tech Trendsetter: Jayendran GS - HousingWire

In January 2026, Jayendran expanded that model with Upfront Income, a universal income platform for agency and non-QM loans. It reviews income documents, performs quality and fraud checks and produces a qualifying income calculation within minutes. It expanded to rental income through a native integration with Fannie Mae’s Income Calculator. The results are significant. Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions increased loan volume by 200%, quadrupled underwriting productivity and improved pull-through from 22% to 65% without adding staff. American Heritage Lending reduced pre-approval time from three hours to 15 minutes and grew loan volume by 300%. Newfi Lending gives brokers qualifying income results in approximately seven minutes, reducing turn times from roughly 72 hours to as little as three. Across its client base, Prudent AI helps lenders move borrowers through their funnels three times faster at 2.5 times lower origination costs. content: Copyright © HT Media Limited  All rights reserved. German two-wheeler manufacturer BMW Motorrad has introduced the new F 450 GS Sport in India at an ex-showroom price of ₹5.90 lakh. Positioned above the existing variants, the new trim brings a revised suspension setup, additional electronic rider aids and an exclusive Racing Red colour option. It comes equipped with several off-road-focused accessories as standard. The F 450 GS Sport is priced ₹25,000 lower than the range-topping GS Trophy variant. One of the key upgrades on the Sport variant is the addition of Sport Suspension, which is aimed at offering improved control and handling across different riding conditions. It also gets Gear Shift Assistant Pro as standard, allowing clutchless gear changes under suitable operating conditions. Another notable addition is the Riding Modes Pro package. Alongside the existing Rain, Road and Enduro settings, it introduces an Enduro Pro mode. The new variant is distinguished by its exclusive Racing Red paint scheme while retaining the F 450 GS's signature X-shaped LED headlamp, front beak and upright adventure-tourer stance. Additionally, the company has equipped it with a clear Rallye windscreen, black handguards, off-road footpegs and a plastic engine guard as standard. The F 450 GS Sport shares several equipment upgrades with the more expensive GS Trophy variant, including Sport Suspension and Riding Modes Pro. However, the two trims differ in certain hardware and convenience features. The GS Trophy gets BMW's Easy Ride Clutch system, which is not offered on the Sport variant. Instead, the latter retains a conventional clutch setup complemented by Gear Shift Assistant Pro. The top-spec GS Trophy also features an aluminium engine guard and a tinted Rallye windscreen, compared to the plastic engine guard and clear windscreen on the Sport. BMW Motorrad India has introduced the new F 450 GS Sport variant in the country with additional equipment aimed at enhancing its sporty and off-road-oriented character, completing the F 450 GS line-up at ₹5.90 lakh (ex-showroom). title: The Adventure Bike That Makes Owning One Motorcycle A Boss Move - Top Speed
content: Motorcycle marketing often promotes the belief that true versatility demands a multi-bike stable: a light thumper for trails, a midweight twin for commuting, and a heavy rig for touring. Managing multiple registrations, insurance policies, and maintenance schedules turns that ideal into an expensive burden. Yet experienced riders know extreme specialization often sacrifices basic usability. Sitting quietly at the premium end of the adventure segment is an understated machine commanding a devoted following because it handles city traffic, cross-country highway miles, and backcountry gravel roads with equal poise, rendering a multi-bike garage unnecessary. The modern full-size adventure segment suffers from a chronic identity crisis, caught between desert-rally marketing and the tarmac reality of long-distance touring. To substantiate rugged off-road claims, manufacturers fit long-travel suspension and 21-inch front wheels to platforms that spend 90 percent of their lives on pavement. On asphalt, that geometry yields vague front-end feedback, slow steering, and crosswind instability. Simultaneously, taming these tall chassis at highway speeds requires massive curb weight and invasive electronics to mask the packaging compromises. Riders face an irritating trade-off: machines too detached and wallowy for spirited cornering, yet far too heavy and intimidating for low-speed technical terrain. Solving this dynamic compromise requires packaging substantial displacement without saddling the motorcycle with a tall roll center. This top-heavy pendulum effect is common to tall V-twin and inline adventure platforms. Placing heavy components as close to the ground as possible dramatically reduces turning inertia. BMW mastered this specific physical balance through its horizontally opposed boxer twin. By positioning the cylinder heads flat and low, BMW drops the core mass beneath knee level, delivering light low-speed handling, straight-line stability on washboard roads, and fatigue-free highway touring. The BMW R 1300 GS gets respect everywhere it goes, because it proves why smart mechanical packaging eliminates the need for separate motorcycles. Combining an ultra-compact boxer layout, under-engine gearbox, and low-slung chassis,it replaces three specialized machines with one integrated platform all for a base price of $20,395. With the optional automatic gearbox, the price climbs to over $25,000, but it manages to be fatigue-free even in traffic. It strips away top-heavy intimidation while retaining all-day touring comfort, establishing itself as the definitive one-bike solution. BMW's 1,300 cc engine looks to be on track to be one of the greats, with its German engineering mastery. It has liquid cooling, four valves per cylinder, BMW ShiftCam on the intake valves that changes both timing and lift, an extremely short stroke design, and a high compression ratio of 13.3:1. It generates 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet at 6,500 RPM, and it has a six-speed manual transmission with an assist-and-slipper clutch. A two-way quickshifter is optional, but the automated manual gearbox (also optional) is what makes it a genuinely great all-round motorcycle. A driveshaft sends power to the rear wheel, which is great for low-maintenance operation. Unlike its competitors, the R 1300 GS uses a unique chassis. This is a pressed-steel monocoque that uses the engine as a stressed member, and the subframe is bolted on. It uses the Evo Telelever wishbone front suspension that offers 7.5 inches of travel and the Paralever central monoshock at the rear with a single-sided swingarm that offers 7.9 inches of travel. Twin 310 mm floating brake discs do duty up front with radial four-piston calipers, and a 285 mm disc at the rear with a two-piston floating caliper. These are mounted on alloy wheels — a 19-inch up front and a 17-inch at the rear — with radial tubeless tires. Tubeless wire-spoke rims are an option, as are more aggressive off-road tires, so you can configure it to feel right at home on any road. The R 1300 GS is a full-size adventure motorcycle, at 87.1 inches long and 39.4 inches wide with a 59.8-inch wheelbase. The seat height is standard for the class at 33.4 inches, and it has a wet weight of 523 pounds. The fuel tank is pretty large even on the regular GS at five gallons; however, with the weight placed down low, it feels a lot lighter than it is, and this feeling is helped by the electronic suspension as well. The features list is packed with everything you would possibly want from a luxury adventure motorcycle. Hop on, and the first thing you will see is the 6.5-inch TFT instrument cluster that has Bluetooth and navigation as standard. The electronics are comprehensive as well, with a by-wire throttle and a six-axis IMU. Of course, you get ride modes, cornering ABS, traction control, and engine brake control, but the optional extras are what truly elevate the big GS. The optional DSA suspension offers automatic damping control, and you can change the rear preload at the touch of a button. This is also one of the few motorcycles that self-levels with a change in load, and the electronic suspension automatically lowers at walking speeds to make it easier to handle. BMW offers different packages for these upgrades, so you will have to check whether the feature you want is available as a standalone one or as part of a package. Be aware that the packages are quite expensive and will easily drive the price to nearly $30,000. This is the sole thing that works against the GS: the high acquisition cost. Otherwise, it eliminates the need for another motorcycle. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. title: US Market Pulse November 2026 - Goldman Sachs Asset Management
content: Global activity remains supported by solid corporate and household balance sheets, AI investment, and fiscal cushions, which offset the dampening effect of tighter monetary policy and higher commodity prices. We expect 2027 growth near 2.5% in the US, and above 1% in Europe and Japan. The FOMC has telegraphed a pace for potential rate hikes of every other meeting. We expect them to raise rates in December, but the move in March will be highly dependent on the data. If inflation continues to normalize, with impulses from energy and tariffs rolling off, we may see them hold at 4.0-4.25%; if pressures broaden, they may have to hike. We expect the ECB to deliver one more hike in December to a peak policy rate of 2.75%. In an election cycle, our focus is not on who wins but rather what a win may change. In the US, a divided government likely means gridlock and more of the same. Upcoming elections in Spain, France, and Italy put a spotlight on fiscal risk, with fractured parliaments less likely to address debt burdens. Government bond yields may stay elevated, as seen recently in French OATs. Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research, and Goldman Sachs Asset Management. As of October 30, 2026. Earnings growth has been exceptional in 2026, boosted by AI investment and higher energy prices. We expect this growth to decelerate in 2027, but to remain supportive of equities. Historically, markets can rally for years past peak earnings growth, though they do become more idiosyncratic. As the AI cycle continues, we would expect focus to be on value capture, quality revenues, and balance sheet strength. Higher rates have led to scrutiny around the funding requirements for AI capex, leading to greater dispersion and spread widening across the AI complex. We remain cautious on IG tech but see scope for some near-term reversal in HY given the scale of the recent selloff. Credit fundamentals are supportive and supply is expected to slow in Q4. Our base case is for energy prices to moderate as supply/demand normalizes and risk premium recedes. However, upside risk remains from possible re-escalation in the Middle East or a colder than expected winter. We also see upward pressure on metals such as copper, where demand from electrification, data centers, and energy security is facing constrained mine supply; and gold, where central bank demand remains robust. title: BMW F 450 GS Sport Launch Price Rs 5.90 Lakh – New Colour, Features - BikeAdvice
content: BMW F 450 GS Sport has been launched in the Indian market at a sticker price of Rs 5.90 lakh (ex-showroom, India). It will be the new range-topping variant in the ADV motorcycle’s line-up as untill now, it was offered in Base, Exclusive and Trophy grades at price points of Rs 4.95 lakh, 5.15 lakh, and Rs 5.60 lakh, respectively. The Sport trim has been rolled out in an exclusive Racing Red paintwork with Sport suspension, Gear Shift Assistant Pro and Riding Modes Pro as standard. The new BMW F 450 GS Sport can be purchased at a monthly installment of just Rs 9,999 per month. First things first, the Racing Red colour scheme is flanked by clear Rallye windscreen and black hand protectors. The off-road footrests and plastic engine guard further amplify the adventure character of the new Sport variant. The F 450 GS is available with standard warranty of three years for unlimited kilometers, and it can be extended to fourth and fifth year as an option. Apart from the new features and paint shade, the F 450 GS Sport remains the same in terms of design and engine specs. Sitting on a a welded tubular steel frame with integrated forged parts, it adorns the same iconic ‘GS’ design philosophy with peculiar styling elements such as the ‘X’ shaped full LED headlight, front beak, split-seat setup, tapered aluminum handlebar and body-coloured side panels. The Base and Exclusive variants are available in Cosmic Black Color scheme while the Trophy variant is presented in Racing Blue Metallic with accents in red and white. It flaunts the tank center cover in Snaefell white paint shade while all the other variants have it in matt black colour scheme. Riding on 19-inch front and 17-inch rear lightweight aluminum wheels, the F 450 GS has been fitted with tubeless tires. BMW F 450 GS comes with four ride modes namely Rain, Road, Enduro and Enduro Pro. Some of the notable safety equipment onboard the ADV bike are ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control, Dynamic Traction Control and Engine Drag Torque Control. A special mention goes to the 6.5-inch TFT display with multicontroller which gets ‘Pure Ride Screen’ and ‘Sport Screen’ displays. The fuel tank capacity stands at 14 litres while the standard saddle height is pegged at 845 mm. At the heart, the F 450 GS houses the newly developed 420cc twin-cylinder inline engine which generates top power of 47 bhp at 8750 rpm and highest torque of 43 Nm at 6750 rpm. The engine is linked to a 6-speed gearbox. The ADV motorcycle is locally produced at TVS factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.

title: BREAKING: BMW F 450 GS Sport Variant Launched In India At Rs 5.90 Lakh - ZigWheels.com
content: The new Sport variant is Rs 25,000 more affordable than the Trophy variant Gets all the other important hardware and features from the Trophy variant BMW Motorrad has launched the F 450 GS Sport variant in India. Until now the variant was not available for the Indian market, and the lineup only consisted of the Base, Exclusive and Trophy variants. Priced at Rs 5.90 (ex-showroom), the new Sport variant is Rs 25,000 more affordable than the Trophy variant. Here is everything you need to know about it. The Sport variant of the BMW F 450 GS comes in a sporty looking glossy red shade that makes the bike look quite striking. This shade could be a good choice for people who want a middle-ground between the funky shade of the Trophy variant, and found the black shade of the Base and Exclusive variants a bit too subtle. This variant also comes equipped with a transparent tall windscreen, a plastic engine guard and black hand guards. Another big difference here is the omission of the Easy Ride Clutch system, which automatically operates the clutch and makes riding in traffic and at low speeds easier. This has made the Sport variant more affordable than the Trophy, while retaining the core adventure touring package. It also comes equipped with fully adjustable sport suspension, with rebound and compression adjustments at the front and rebound and preload adjustments at the rear. This variant also gets off-road centric footpegs for better control while tackling rough roads. The F 450 GS Sport continues to use the same 420 cc parallel-twin liquid-cooled engine producing 48 PS, 43 Nm and comes paired to a 6-speed gearbox with slipper clutch. It also retains the 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheel setup along with dual-purpose tyres. In terms of equipment, the motorcycle gets switchable dual channel ABS, switchable traction control, a 6.5-inch TFT console and Gear Shift Assistant Pro. The BMW F 450 GS Sport makes sense for buyers who want the performance, electronics and adventure-ready hardware of the top-spec Trophy edition without paying extra for the Easy Ride Clutch. Although the ERC does work quite seamlessly, however, it does make the bike feel slightly lazier, and it’s something purists won't like. Without the ERC the bike is also expected to perform slightly better, and now it could be the sweet spot in the range, especially for experienced riders who prefer a conventional clutch setup. title: BMW F 450 GS Sport Launched at Rs. 5.90 Lakh - BikeWale
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the new F 450 GS Sport in India at Rs. 5.90 lakh (ex-showroom) sitting above the existing variants bringing in revised suspension package, additional electronic equipment and an exclusive Racing Red paint scheme. It also receives off-road-focused accessories as standard making it a more specialised version of the F 450 GS. It sits Rs. 25,000 below the GS Trophy questioning you about which version offers better value. The biggest change is the introduction of Sport Suspension which will offer improved control with a more focused setup than the standard version. F 450 GS Sport also receives Gear Shift Assistant Pro as standard allowing riders to change gears without operating the clutch under appropriate conditions. title: Chef Jeremy Fox Brings Birdie G’s To Fairmont Century Plaza As L.A. Landmark Celebrates 60th Anniversary - Maxim
content: The Los Angeles mid-century classic welcomes an all-day American brasserie, special cocktails, and luxury wellness rituals for its 60th birthday. When Jeremy Fox first launched Birdie G’s in 2019, the dining concept was rooted in a blend of Midwestern supper club nostalgia, Southern hospitality, and California’s hyper-seasonal ethos. Now, the James Beard–nominated chef is evolving his restaurant into a bustling, all-day American brasserie at L.A.’s Fairmont Century Plaza. Designed in partnership with EDG Design, the space aims to shift from early-morning espressos to power lunches and hearty dinners as it launches a new culinary option for Century City. Named after Fox’s daughter Birdie and grandmother Gladys, the eatery reimagines classic comfort foods through expert technique and local sourcing. Dinner options include hearth-cooked, koji-marinated prime steaks, lamb “à la Saless” with fenugreek and beet molasses, steak tartare, and matzo ball soup enriched with carrot miso. Desserts are led by a signature Rose Petal Pie tucked inside a salty-sweet pretzel crust and a warm Sticky Date Bundt Cake doused in rich caramel. The restaurant’s design strikes a balance between mid-century elegance and warm 1970s revival, featuring custom leather finishes, warm rust tones, and green plaid bar stools that reference the exact interior of Fox’s first 1969 Volkswagen Beetle. Fox notes that this setting finally captures the soul of the concept, creating the sensation of stepping out of a sleek hotel lobby directly into an elevated supper club. The opening marks a pivotal addition to the Fairmont Century Plaza as the storied property celebrates its 60th anniversary. Built on a former 20th Century Fox backlot and designed by architect Minoru Yamasaki, the crescent-shaped hotel opened on June 1, 1966, packed with then-futuristic luxuries like built-in vanities and color televisions. Over the decades, it became an epicenter for cultural and political history. The Beatles celebrated their wins here at the 10th Annual Grammy Awards, and President Richard Nixon hosted a 1969 “Dinner of the Century” to honor the Apollo 11 astronauts. During the 1980s, President Ronald Reagan visited so frequently that the press dubbed the property the “Western White House.” Following a massive $2.5 billion transformation led by Yabu Pushelberg, the hotel updated its classic mid-century architecture while still maintaining its old-school status. The property now features 400 residential-style guest rooms with private balconies, a rooftop pool offering sweeping views across Los Angeles, and a expansive 14,000-square-foot spa facility. To mark six decades of luxury hospitality, the hotel is launching a series of anniversary activations running through December 31. Guests can book the Celebrate The Century Package for champagne on arrival and valet parking, or order from the Sip The Century cocktail menu at The Bar, where each drink takes inspiration from a notable decade or guest. For wellness travelers, the spa offers a Diamond Legacy Facial, a $546 sculpting treatment developed by 111SKIN that utilizes diamond absorption tech to firm and illuminate the skin. General Manager Hiren Prabhakar noted that the L.A. property’s longevity lies in its ability to continuously redefine the local hospitality landscape: “As Los Angeles evolves, so does Fairmont Century Plaza, continuing to shape the luxury hospitality experience through exceptional dining, meaningful partnerships, and distinctive experiences that bring people together,” he said in a statement to Maxim. “The addition of Birdie G’s by Chef Jeremy Fox is another reflection of our continued evolution and commitment to bringing new experiences to the property.”

title: ADVENTURE | BMW R 1300 GS PURE - ADB Magazine
content:
There are worse ways to conduct a motorcycle debrief than sitting outside a café with a coffee and a curry pie. Jeremy Cowley had just returned from three solid days of interstate riding aboard BMW’s R 1300 GS Pure, so rather than ask him to sit down and type 2000 words about it, I figured I’d shout him lunch and hit record. Besides, after that many kilometres aboard BMW’s big boxer, his arse had probably spent enough time sitting down. Plus, do you know how hard it is for a journo to get his wallet out! Cowley is becoming our resident adventure-bike tragic whether he likes the title or not. He owns a Husqvarna Norden 901 and a 2006 KTM 950 Super Enduro, has ridden everything from the Royal Enfield Himalayan and Honda CRF300 Rally to the CFMOTO 450MT-X, and there’s plenty more big-bore ADV experience in the family. His old man has owned a Triumph Tiger 800 and now has a Tiger 1200. The GS Pure is an interesting proposition. This isn’t the fully loaded, everything-and-the-kitchen-sink GS most people picture when they hear BMW. It’s the stripped-back entry point into the R 1300 GS family, but it still gets the 1300cc ShiftCam boxer producing a whopping 107kW and 149Nm, along with electronic suspension adjustment, riding modes, a quickshifter, TFT display, keyless ignition and laced wheels. In other words, ‘Pure’ doesn’t exactly mean you’re starting the bloody thing with a kickstarter. So, with coffee in hand and the curry pie rapidly disappearing, I started with the obvious question. JEREMY: Big. And weird. I’ve never really spent much time on BMWs before, so the first thing I noticed was that motor hanging out either side. I’m a massive boxer fan from driving and racing Subarus, so I understand the concept and actually love that engine configuration, but on a motorcycle it’s strange when you’re not used to it. Normally you look down on an adventure bike and see a tank or dual tanks, but on the BMW you look down and there are two bloody cylinder heads sticking out the sides. Once you’re on it, though, it immediately feels like a nice motorcycle. Sometimes with a base-model bike you can tell where the manufacturer has saved money with maybe cheaper bars, slightly ordinary ergonomics or something that makes it feel like the povo-pack version but I didn’t really get that from the Pure. The riding position was comfortable, everything felt quality and after three big days aboard it, I wasn’t looking for an excuse to throw it in a ditch. JEREMY: Bugger me. There is just so much power. It’s that huge wave of torque where you can be cruising along in fourth gear, decide you want to disappear and it just motors. I’ve ridden some seriously fast big adventure bikes now and, for me, the power delivery from this thing was better than any of them. On the road it was beautiful, and I honestly reckon I could ride that thing around Australia. Long highway days, big open roads and huge distances are where that engine makes complete sense because you’ve always got this ridiculous amount of effortless power sitting underneath you. But I reckon it’s almost too much off-road. You’ve got 145 horsepower in an adventure bike and at some point you’ve got to ask yourself what the hell you’re supposed to do with all of it. Nobody needs that much horsepower on a dirt road. Nobody. JEREMY:  I reckon the definition of an adventure bike has changed. On the dirt, I felt like I was having to work for it more than I wanted to. That’s not because the GS is bad; it’s because it’s a massive, hugely powerful motorcycle and this particular Pure isn’t really set up to be a hardcore off-road weapon. It still has plenty of technology to make it manageable, but if I wanted to get serious in the dirt I’d start with tyres and then probably look at the suspension to get it working a little better for that sort of riding. But I don’t think that’s what this bike is trying to be. We’re talking big gravel roads, corrugations, fire trails and stuff where you’re travelling rather than trying to find the nastiest singletrack possible. Put some decent tyres on it and I’d happily point it down that sort of road all day. MITCH: Like a lounge chair you can take down the Oodnadatta Track? JEREMY: Exactly. A really bloody fast lounge chair. JEREMY: No. That boxer engine looks enormous because you’ve got those cylinders hanging out the sides, but all that weight is sitting low. Once the bike is moving it feels much lighter than you’d expect, and when you’re flowing along a road it disguises its size incredibly well. It was probably the nicest adventure-roadie-tourer-whatever-you-want-to-call-it I’ve ridden on the highway. The front-end was another thing. It’s BMW’s Telelever setup and apparently I’m supposed to have some grand opinion on that. Honestly, I didn’t. I probably wouldn’t have mentioned it because there was nothing strange about the way it behaved – it just worked. JEREMY: Fine. The rider triangle felt good sitting or standing and I never really had an ergonomic issue with it. Wind protection was decent too. It’s nowhere near the worst adventure bike I’ve ridden for buffeting although you could fit a bigger screen if you were doing huge touring kilometres. The Pure doesn’t have that giant touring screen, but again, that’s part of what this model is. The only thing that annoyed me was BMW’s scroll-wheel controller on the left grip. I’m not a fan of those systems on bikes generally, so it’s not really a BMW-specific whinge. It works, I just reckon there are simpler ways of doing it. MITCH: ARE BIG-BORE ADVENTURE BIKES BECOMING TOURERS? JEREMY: I think once you get into the 1200 and 1300cc stuff now, you’re really moving towards touring. Look at the bikes around 900cc, you can ride those things all day on the road without a drama, but they’re still bloody capable when you get properly off-road. My KTM 950 Super Enduro is a 2006 model and the 950/990 generation is still regarded by plenty of people as some of the best adventure bikes KTM ever made. It’s funny because the market spent years moving towards 1200 and 1300cc bikes, and now we’re almost coming back around to that 900-ish capacity because it’s such a good compromise. JEREMY: Tyres first, depending on what I was doing. My 950 has a proper aggressive off-road tyre because when I use that bike it’s generally at an event where I know I’m going into the dirt. My Norden 901 has more of a 70/30 tyre because I actually ride it on the road to get places, and when I hit the dirt I’ll drop a couple of psi and get on with it. That’s probably exactly how I’d approach the BMW. If you’re doing 70 per cent bitumen to get to 30 per cent dirt, there’s no point fitting a massive aggressive knob and destroying it at highway speeds before you’ve even reached the fun stuff. The sort of person buying a GS in Sydney, Melbourne or Canberra is probably going to spend a fair chunk of every adventure just getting out of town. JEREMY: Yep. The Pure has Eco, Rain, Road and Enduro modes, and Rain mode is actually really nice on the dirt. It takes the edge off the throttle and gives you some slip without letting the thing completely light up, which isn’t a bad idea when you’ve got a 1300cc boxer trying to fire you at the horizon. Dad used Rain mode quite a bit and I can understand why. A lot of adventure riders do the same thing. You don’t necessarily need maximum aggression just because you’ve left the bitumen; sometimes making a huge motorcycle softer and easier to manage actually lets you ride it faster and with less effort. And that, really, is where we landed once the coffees were empty and Cowley had demolished the pie. The R 1300 GS Pure isn’t pretending to be a 1300cc enduro bike, and perhaps we’ve reached the point where we need to stop expecting enormous adventure motorcycles to be one. Its job is to smash out huge distances in ridiculous comfort, make 145 horsepower feel effortless and let you keep going when the bitumen ends. For that job, Cowley reckons BMW has built a bloody good thing. title: TikTok Is Turning Karol G’s Album Release Into a Live Fan Event - WeRSM
content: TikTok is making Karol G’s album release a live appointment. On November 4, the Colombian artist will perform songs from No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto in a one-hour TikTok LIVE Premiere, streamed from 8:00 to 9:00 PM Mexico City time. The event will run on Karol G’s official TikTok account, giving her audience a shared moment around an album that has already reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart. The platform’s official announcement positions the livestream as more than a concert broadcast. It is a way to connect a major music release directly to the fan behavior TikTok has helped create. Karol G has more than 56 million followers on TikTok, while “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido” has appeared in more than 1.7 million user-created videos. That gives TikTok something most music platforms cannot easily replicate: a visible, active layer of participation around the artist and her songs. The livestream brings that participation into the release moment itself. Fans in Medellín and Madrid can watch the same performance at the same time, with comments running alongside the set. The audience is not only consuming the album. It is reacting publicly and collectively as the artist performs it. TikTok has already tested this broader release playbook with Karol G. Around her 2025 album Tropicoqueta, the platform created an AI Karol G effect, themed profile frames, and a leaderboard ranking countries by views of related content. LIVE Premiere adds a real-time layer to that existing system of effects, posts, fandom signals, and discovery. That matters because TikTok is moving closer to the center of the music launch, not simply serving as the place where songs become popular after release. With LIVE Premiere, the platform can help shape the moment itself, then let fans extend it through comments, clips, reactions, and new videos. For artists, the value is a tighter connection between attention and participation. For TikTok, it is another reason for fans to stay inside the app when a cultural moment is happening. The album remains the product, but the live community response becomes part of the release strategy.

title: Global Music Revenues Are Forecast to Rise as Subscriber Growth Beats Expectations - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Global music industry revenues are expected to reach approximately $200 billion annually by 2035 amid an improving outlook for subscription streaming. New subscription models, AI, and direct-to-consumer offerings are creating opportunities for the industry to reach audiences in new ways, according to Goldman Sachs Research. The music market undershot growth expectations over the last several years. The new forecast represents the first time in three years that Goldman Sachs Research has raised its long-term outlook for the industry, Stephen Laszczyk and Eric Sheridan write in the team’s 2026 edition of the annual “Music in the Air” report. Goldman Sachs Research expects global music revenues to increase at 6.7% year-on-year in 2026 and at a compound rate of 5.8% per year between 2025 and 2035. “While growth is likely to moderate from the pace observed during the industry's streaming adoption phase, we continue to see a long runway for industry expansion supported by favorable consumer behavior and an increasingly diversified monetization model,” Laszczyk and Sheridan write. Music streaming subscriptions are growing faster than expected Paid streaming subscriptions are helping to shore up the outlook for recorded music. After three consecutive downgrades to its forecast for 2030 recorded music revenues, Goldman Sachs Research’s outlook for the segment this year reflects improvements in streaming revenue, physical revenue, and download and other digital revenue. Subscription streaming revenue is growing faster, mainly because subscriber numbers are increasing more quickly than expected and revenue per user is rising in developed markets. Our analysts are factoring in more consistent price increases from streaming platforms as music labels increasingly incorporate higher royalties into their contracts and streaming platforms introduce new premium service tiers. At the same time, increasing fan demand for vinyl and CDs is helping lift the outlook for physical music revenues in markets like Japan, South Korea, and the US. “We expect these trends to continue as fans increasingly view physical formats as collectibles rather than as a way to listen, and as artists incorporate physical formats into their album rollouts and tour experiences,” Laszczyk and Sheridan write. Paid subscription streaming revenue beat our analysts’ expectations in 2025, and Goldman Sachs Research expects further growth ahead, driven by emerging markets. Laszczyk and Sheridan forecast the percentage of internet users with paid streaming subscriptions in emerging markets to rise from 10% in 2025 to 15% in 2035, with subscriber numbers boosted by growing populations and increasing internet penetration. Paid subscriptions in developed markets also have room to grow, according to Laszczyk and Sheridan, who expect the number of paid subscribers in the US, Canada, Europe, and Australasia to rise to 568 million in 2035 from 398 million in 2025. Only around 53% of Americans subscribed to paid music streaming in 2025, compared with around 60% for gaming and 90% for on-demand video. Goldman Sachs Research expects most developed markets to approach peak penetration for paid music streaming at 60% by 2035. Older age groups and new products could help drive paid music users Older listeners could be an untapped audience. Data from the UK shows that older listeners are less likely to use paid streaming and less likely to convert from free to paid users. “We see opportunity for increased conversion from free to paid among older age groups, especially as younger age cohorts who are heavy users of paid streaming services grow older, and as streaming providers adapt their marketing strategies to target older demographics,” Laszczyk and Sheridan write. Introducing an ad-light tier could also help streaming providers drive subscriber acquisition. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that a small incremental fee of around $1-2 per month for a reduced advertising load could result in subscriber growth. “This follows a similar playbook to what has already been implemented in video streaming,” Laszczyk and Sheridan observe. If 10% of free streaming users in developed markets shifted to a $1 ad-light tier, global ad-supported revenues would rise by around 8%, Goldman Sachs Research estimates. Another emerging opportunity in streaming is direct-to-consumer offerings, where artists build a direct relationship with their fans without an intermediary platform controlling access to that audience. This innovation is still in its early stages, Laszczyk and Sheridan write. But “if this ecosystem continues to develop the way it has been, the direct-to-consumer opportunity could grow from representing tens of millions of dollars of revenue today to hundreds of millions over the next decade.” Increased touring and new venues are buoying live music Despite pressure on consumer wallets from tariffs, gasoline prices, and higher interest rates, our analysts expect the market for live music to grow 6% in 2026, driven by a strong global arena and stadium business. This supports Goldman Sachs Research’s thesis that demand for live events has increased globally since the Covid-19 pandemic, and that the sector is less exposed to economic downturns than other forms of discretionary spending. Looking ahead, our analysts expect live music to grow at a similar 6% compound rate through 2035, underpinned by an increasing supply of diverse and popular artists touring over the next decade. Stronger financial incentives to tour and efforts by record labels to promote new talent are set to drive the live music sector, Laszczyk and Sheridan project. And they expect venue capacity to grow, with operators poised to open several dozen new music venues around the world in the next five to seven years. AI’s impact on the music industry has been “the biggest debate among music investors over the last year,” Laszczyk and Sheridan say. One concern is that AI-generated music will displace human artists, but Laszczyk and Sheridan believe that fear is overblown for higher-profile artists in the near term. While the team does see some potential for cannibalization by AI over the long term, they expect that it will mostly be limited to lower-value music (including background and study music as well as mid-tier artists). Only a mid-single-digit percentage of consumers used an AI music generation tool at least monthly as of the fourth quarter of 2025. As of the third quarter of 2025, around 55% of music creators had used an AI tool in the past year, but mostly for production workflow or mastering rather than to generate entirely new songs. At the same time, AI represents an opportunity for music labels and rights holders: Streaming providers and tech companies can use the technology to personalize recommendations, curate content, and turn passive listeners into active creators. “We believe that monetization will ultimately make its way back to the rights holders in a way that we think will disproportionately benefit some of these higher-end artists where AI music is likely created off of their image and likeness, their melodies, or their lyrics, given how popular they are,” Laszczyk says. China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) has leaked the official product images and filing data for the upcoming Buick Electra GS plug-in hybrid sedan. Developed by the SAIC-GM joint venture, the large, fastback-style sedan is tailored specifically for the Chinese market and is very unlikely to ever set wheels on American land due to regulatory hurdles and prohibitive tariffs. The production version represents a significant departure from the much taller, hatchback-like Electra GS Concept that made its debut in April 2025 as a preview of a future production model. And this is it! It may not be the concept car’s identical twin, but it is the next best thing. With styling that pays tribute to Buick’s iconic Gran Sport lineup, the Electra GS PHEV car features ultra-slim, C-shaped LED headlights linked by an LED strip. The Buick tri-shield logo sits right below on a less aggressive "shark-nose" front fascia. The Electra GS is the slightly shorter and potentially more affordable alternative to Buick’s existing Electra L7 Sportback sedan. It measures 190.0 inches (4,980 millimeters) in length, 75.4 inches (1,915 millimeters) in width, and 58.9 inches (1,495 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 112.8 inches (2,865 millimeters). Those numbers make it slightly smaller than the Buick Electra L7. The leaked documents confirm the plug-in hybrid setup, which combines the electric motor, good for 221 horsepower (224 metric horsepower), with either the naturally aspirated 1.5-liter or the turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-four. The naturally aspirated engine produces 72 horsepower (73 metric horsepower, while the turbocharged unit churns out 154 horsepower (156 metric horsepower). The base variant rolls off the production line with 318 horsepower (322 metric horsepower), while the range-topping turbocharged example sees the light of day with a combined system output of 375 horsepower (380 metric horsepower). GM hasn’t revealed any pricing details either, but it will most likely happen closer to the launch date set for early 2027. While the Buick Electra GS PHEV will stay away from the U.S., it has every chance to make it to the European market.
