title: Buick Electra GS appears in China regulatory filing, expanding NEV lineup - CnEVPost
content: Buick's Electra GS plug-in hybrid sedan has appeared in China's latest regulatory filing catalog, revealing the fastback model's exterior and key powertrain specifications. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology released its 413th batch of new vehicle filings on Tuesday, with public comments open from November 4 to 10. The Electra GS has 3 variants in the filings, all manufactured by SAIC-GM, covering 2 engine options and different battery cell suppliers. Buick is a brand under General Motors (NYSE: GM). All 3 variants feature an electric motor with a peak output of 165 kW (221 hp). Their engines each have a displacement of 1,498 milliliters, with rated outputs of 72 kW for 2 variants and 115 kW for the remaining variant. All 3 variants use lithium iron phosphate batteries. One uses cells supplied by Rept Battero Energy (HKEX: 666), while the other 2 use cells from Zenergy. Battery packs for all variants are produced by a SAIC-GM subsidiary. The filings do not list battery capacity or electric range. Filing images show the Electra GS with a coupe-like fastback profile, slim headlights, a full-width taillight and semi-hidden door handles, along with Electra GS badging at the rear. The 5-seat sedan measures 4,979 mm in length and 1,914 mm in width, with a wheelbase of 2,865 mm. Height varies slightly across the filed variants. The images show roof-mounted LiDAR, while the filings also list an option without LiDAR, alongside choices of rear spoilers, brake calipers and exterior trim. The filings do not disclose the supplier or specific capabilities of the driver-assistance system, nor do they detail final trim levels, pricing or launch timing. The Electra GS filing comes as Buick continues to update its new energy vehicle (NEV) lineup in China. On September 23, the brand launched an updated Electra E7 plug-in hybrid SUV, just 5 months after its initial launch. The Electra E7 update focused on powertrain and driver-assistance equipment, with the Pro trim combining a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine and advanced driver-assistance features. title: Former CEO of SGX-listed GS Holdings charged over false trading - The Business Times
content: Now known as Octopus (Apac) Holdings, the company has expanded into beverage distribution [SINGAPORE] The former CEO of GS Holdings, Pang Pok, was charged in court on Wednesday (Nov 4) with abetting a conspiracy to engage in share price manipulation and perverting the course of justice, said the Singapore Police Force. Pang, 68, who stepped down as CEO in 2024, is accused of conspiring with Koh Kim Seng, 62, and Chong Fatt, 60, to create a misleading appearance with respect to the price of GS Holdings’ securities between January 2022 and October 2023. The court documents did not state what roles Koh and Chong held in the company. Pang and Chong are also accused of deleting chat messages from their mobile phones relating to the alleged conspiracy. They face an additional charge of perverting the course of justice. All three men face, among other charges, one count each under the Securities and Futures Act. GS Holdings – behind several foodcourts and food centres in Singapore – was renamed  Octopus (Apac) Holdings  : 43A 0% in February 2026 and is listed on the Catalist board of the Singapore Exchange. The charges arose from a joint investigation by the Commercial Affairs Department of the Singapore Police Force and the Monetary Authority of Singapore, following a referral from Singapore Exchange Regulation. If convicted, the accused face imprisonment of up to seven years, a fine of up to S$250,000, or both, for each charge relating to false trading. The penalty for perverting the course of justice includes imprisonment of up to seven years, a fine, or both. The charges come amid a series of corporate developments at Octopus (Apac) Holdings. The company appointed Paul Hopkins, formerly general manager of Maritime and Mercantile Asia Pacific, as its group CEO in October 2025. He stepped down from the role after less than a year, on Jul 21, 2026. The group’s expansion into beverage distribution began earlier in 2025. In May that year, it acquired Octopus Distribution Networks (ODN), which has since become the main focus of its F&B distribution business. ODN subsequently expanded its portfolio in September 2025 by agreeing to acquire the distribution business of LHA Food & Beverages for about S$3 million in cash. The transaction included the rights to distribute 11 Degree Premium Yanjing Beer in Singapore, as well as the trademarks of Rossl Bier and Como Bere. In February 2026, the company changed its name to Octopus (Apac) Holdings, to better reflect the business profile and strategic direction. The company entered into a conditional share sale-and-purchase agreement to dispose of its entire stake in wholly owned subsidiary Hawkerway to Wei Global for a net cash consideration of S$650,000. title: Former CEO of GS Holdings, firm behind foodcourts in S’pore, facing false trading charge - The Straits Times
content: Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox Pang Pok (left), 68, who stepped down as chief executive in 2024, is said to have conspired with two others - Chong Fatt (middle), 60, and Koh Kim Seng, 62 (right). SINGAPORE – The former chief executive of public-listed GS Holdings, a firm behind several foodcourts and food centres in Singapore, is facing a charge over allegations of share price manipulation. Pang Pok, 68, who stepped down as CEO in 2024, is said to have conspired with two others – Chong Fatt, 60, and Koh Kim Seng, 62 – to create a misleading appearance of the price of GS Holdings, whose shares were traded on the Catalist board of the Singapore Exchange. It was not stated in court documents what roles Chong and Koh had in GS Holdings. According to court documents, the three men allegedly pushed up the price of the firm’s securities by using three trading accounts to place orders and execute trades for GS Holdings’ securities between January 2022 and October 2023. Pang and Chong are also accused of perverting the course of justice by deleting text messages relating to the trades. All three men did not enter a plea on Nov 4. Their cases were adjourned to Dec 2 for them to engage lawyers. Pang’s bail amount was set at $120,000, while Chong’s was set at $40,000 and Koh’s at $30,000. According to SGX filings, GS Holdings changed its name earlier in 2026 to Octopus (APAC) Holdings to represent its ambition to become a leading food and beverage distribution partner in the Asia-Pacific region. Those convicted of committing false trading can be jailed for up to seven years, fined up to $250,000, or both. If found guilty of perverting the course of justice, an individual can be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both. Nadine Chua is a correspondent covering crime and court at The Straits Times.
